Here's a list of things to consider when detangling: •Start with the right tools: get a detangling brush with wide-tooth bristles to gently work through tangles without damaging the hair. •Use the right products: Depending on the condition of the hair —use a leave-in detangling spray or a conditioner that's not so heavy and has some slip to help soften and hydrate the hair. Dry detangling could result in an excessive amount of breakage. •Section the hair into manageable sections to maintain control and efficiency. Always start detangling from bottom and work your way up the hair shaft. If finger detangling; separate hair horizontally to prevent breaking hair up the shaft. • Be gentle, be patient, be kind to your hair. PART 1: Do you have rounded shoulders?  Typically along with this you may notice your head comes forward or your back is a little hunched. Maybe you also experienced neck tension, headaches or jaw pain? But then again, you don’t have to experience any of that, but you can still have rounded shoulders. Some people want to get out of pain while others just want to look normal and not like a gorilla. There are a few areas of the body we have to look at specifically the glenohumeral, joint, a.k.a. shoulder, joint, the scapula, a.k.a. shoulder blade and the thoracic spine, a.k.a. upper back. We also need to look down the chain to the hips and core as well. If you can take a systematic approach, balancing out the restrictions or tightness on one side of the joint while simultaneously building strength on the other side of the joint you can get yourself to a better position and keep yourself there.  In this video, I show how do I address the shoulder joint, the shoulder blade and the thoracic spine with a total of six exercises. In Part Two which posts after this video, I will show a great hip exercise, which can build a foundation for you to be successful in maintaining an upright posture, and stop looking like a gorilla with rounded shoulders.  #posture #roundedshoulders #forwardheadposture #neckpain #headaches #migraines #tmj #shouldermobility #stretching

Have you noticed that your jaw shifts to the side during opening? It does not open in a straight line and maybe there is pain or aching associated with it? Well, typically, this is one of two things, muscle imbalances or joint dysfunction. In this video, we focus on the muscle dysfunction side of things. Anytime there is muscle imbalance or unilateral movement. We need to figure out what are the spasming or tight muscle muscles that pull it one way and what are the weak muscles that we need to build up to pull it back the other direction. In this video I show you how to release the lateral pterygoid muscle as it is the primary muscle responsible for shifting your jaw to the opposite direction and when there is spasm in one of these muscles, you will excessively shift in the opposite direction.  And then we focus on strengthening the four muscles that force it to move away from the shift back to neutral alignment….which are the lateral pterygoid and medial pterygoid on the side of the shift, as well as the temporalis and masseter on the opposite  side. Confused yet? This is a great starting point for you and if you don’t have the results you want and you notice sharp pains or clicking and popping, it may actually be a joint issue and you’ll have to tune back in for another video on that. #tmj #tmjdisorder #tmd #dentisty #dentist

In Native American and indigenous culture hair is more than just hair or a style. For different nations and tribes hair is considered a connection to creator and the spiritual world. Many natives are against cutting their hair and keep their hair in braids as part of that. They may only cut it when mourning or for other ceremonial reasons. This does vary by tribe as Native Americans are not a monolith so each tribe or nation may have its own beliefs regarding hair. Considering Native American and indigenous identity remember that hair is something that’s important and sometimes sacred and not just a Style. #nativetiktok #nativefamily #nativeamerican

Day 46: 700 miles in. Kennedy Meadows. This was a big one. 700 miles on foot from Mexico to here. Kennedy Meadows marks the start of the Sierra Nevada. A month at high altitude, big climbs, big snow, big adventure. I’ve been dreaming of this stretch since day 1. But first—breakfast was a single Clif bar and a few sad bits of dried fruit. Swung by the Kern River for a dip… it would’ve swept me away. Hit the 700-mile marker. Got emotional. Got hungry. Walked straight into Kennedy Meadows—only to find the general store closed. BUT Jelly, absolute wizard, had stashed his car here before the hike and predicted his arrival date to the day. We jumped in and hit Grumpy’s for food. Rocket Shoes made it memorable by absolutely destroying an egg. Town wasn’t quite awake yet, so we made the call—back to San Jacinto to finish the last section we missed. One more chapter before the Sierra begins. Drive was too long after that stretch, so we stopped half way in tehachapi at the wonderful trial angels we stayed on the way north.  Feet are tired. Belly’s full. Desert = done. Sierra = coming. Let’s keep moving. #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california #pctgrant #thruhiking #desert #pct #snow #sierra #hikertrash

Day 18: Today was one of those days that tests you. A long, exhausting 10-mile grind through a dry creek bed—except it wasn’t so dry. Heavy rains had destroyed the main trail, leaving behind a mess of loose rock, deep sand, and washed-out sections that felt more like an obstacle course than a path. At times, it was downright dangerous, scrambling over unstable terrain with no clear route forward. Every step took focus. Every mile felt like two. Mission Creek was a much-needed break. Food, water, a moment to reset. But I couldn’t stay long—I wanted to push higher before nightfall. Three more miles, climbing up through fresh snow, every breath thinner as I gained altitude. Finally, at 8,000 feet, I set up camp, legs burning, body wrecked, but mind locked in. Two more days to Big Bear. Tomorrow is going to be brutal, but I’ve come too far to let up now. The only way is forward. 242.2/2650 miles.    #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california #desert #snow #pct #thruhiking #pctgrant

Do you experience headaches especially right above the ear? Maybe it feels like an intense pressure or tension? Particularly clenching and grinding, can produce pain above the ear and in this video I show a simple test to determine if that’s you. You see when you clench your your temporalis muscle, the one above the ear, tightens up, and it can produce pain, but if you shift your jaw forward slightly, and then attempt to clench, you cannot generate the same contraction. So if clenching reproduces your headache pain, but then shifting forward and clenching no longer produce it as well that can be a sign that your headaches are coming from clenching. From there, there are several different ways to address it, but one would be repositioned of the jaw at night so you cannot get a good clench and in this video, I explained how an NTI can be used for that! #tmj #tmd #tmjdisorder #tmjtreatment #jawpain #tmj #dental #dentistry

Day 23: I had a secret side mission today… It started with coffee in my sleeping bag, because some mornings you just need a slow start. Then came the miles—smooth trail, sunshine, and for a brief moment, the illusion that today would be easy. Then came the trees. So many trees. Climbing, jumping, crawling—turns out the trail had other plans. A Pop-Tart helped morale. A river crossing tested my patience. Hiking miles off-trail just to find WiFi… because priorities. The reward? A burger, a milkshake, and the realization that maybe eating that much, that fast, wasn’t my best decision. Nothing a freezing creek dip couldn’t fix. Fresh start. New man. And just in time for a sunset that made every step worth it. Would I do it again? Absolutely. 298.5/2650 miles. Day 69: Lost Liam, gained Pablo. That’s trail math. Yesterday we hammered out 23 snowy miles and made it to camp just in time for Liam to peace out and keep hiking into the night. Wild. Now we’re three, Pablo’s officially joined the squad, and we’re hoping NorCal cuts us a break with some dry trail. Spoiler: it tried. Started the day with freezing creek water and a river lit by sunrise. Saw Liam’s prints in the snow like some ghost of big miles past. Then… dry trail. Real, actual, beautiful dirt. First time in a while it felt like the PCT. Even saw some bear prints, good reminder we’re not alone out here. Rolled into Sierra City for a quick pit stop, 1.3 miles off-trail but worth it. Burgers, sockets, and mileage marker sign. Then came the climb. Endless switchbacks, even the water source was mocking us: “Switchback Spring.” Views at the top were something else, dry ridges, snowy peaks… and then back into the slush for the final few miles. I was skiing in trail runners to save my knees. Dinner? Pinnacle creamy Tuscan chicken. Elite. Sunset over a lake with no ice, finally. What a day. #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california #pctgrant #desert #thruhiking #pct #snow #hikertrash

Day 44: 25 miles 3 days to Kennedy Meadows and the rocks are getting personal. Started before sunrise with the headtorch on, chasing miles before the heat hit. Passed a bag of books on trail (??), hit a trail register and a water cache, and saw a historical point of interest that turned out to be a Prius in the desert. Classic… Wildflowers were popping off, but so were my feet. The trail climbed, the views hit, then came the rocks. Again. Always the rocks. Detoured for water at Joshua Tree Spring, then collapsed under some shade very dramatically. Managed to pull it together for the final push. Feet ruined. Clothes drying. Tent zipped. Day 30: Soggy Tent, Rocket Shoes & a Stormy Night Woke up to a wet tent. Not just damp-soaked. Love that for me. Nothing like packing up a waterlogged shelter to really set the tone for the day. Started strong with second breakfast: a Pop-Tart. Elite fuel. Then hit the trail, legs feeling heavy but still moving. A long climb early on made sure I was fully awake-steep, slow, and questioning my choices-but the view at the top made it worth it. A few miles in, I spotted a tree that clearly lost a fight with lightning, a rock that had to be a cat, and a burn area warning just to keep things interesting. Somewhere along the way, I completely missed the 400-mile marker. So we're celebrating 400.9 miles instead. Close enough. Trail snacks kept morale high-Sour Patch Kids for motivation, a mid-day burrito for pure joy. And at some point, I even ran? Rocket shoes unlocked?? Rolled into camp first (rare), but no water meant pushing another two miles. Grabbed a quick resupply, did some emergency sleeping pad surgery, and then watched storm clouds roll in. Now I'm lying here in my flapping tent, listening to the wind rage, hoping I don't get launched into the night. Sleep? Probably not happening. See you for Day 31... if I'm still here. #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california #desert #pctgrant #thruhiking #pct #hikertrash

Day 29: Sketchy Trails & Indiana Jones Moves Started the day with an Instagram follower who joined for a section—respect to them for sending it up, but coming down alone was too risky, so they made the smart call to turn back. Me and the boys kept pushing through the sketchy scree, nothing but loose rock and careful footwork until we finally hit solid trail. From there, we cranked up the pace. Endless climbs, a long road diversion that felt like it would never end, then back into the mountains as the clouds rolled in. A couple of dogs came over to check us out when we got back on trail, right before we passed a sign casually reminding us about mountain lions and rattlesnakes—good times. Then came the highlight: crossing a river on a massive fallen tree, full-on Indiana Jones style. One last brutal climb to Cooper Canyon, and finally, we called it a day. Absolutely wrecked, but still moving forward.  17 miles today. This Big Red Barbacoa made from @H-E-B sourced beef cheeks is everything I hoped for the first time—and didn’t quite land (follow me on Instagram and scroll back if you want receipts lol).  Huge shoutout to @Hurtado Barbecue for the in-depth breakdown that turned this cook into a certified comeback. Started by picking up some quality cheeks from HEB—always look for solid marbling and clean sinew lines. Spent the time to trim off that hard cartilage so all you’re left with is pure, buttery goodness.  From there, I built out the beef blend straight from Brandon’s book (same one he uses at his restaurants) and hit it with a heavy hand of seasoning before letting it sit overnight. Fired up the @Char-Griller offset with straight post oak splits and lit it up easy with @StumpChunks —the GOAT of fire starters.  Once that peppery bark set in and we hit the 180° mark, it was braise time: rich beef stock and a full pour of #BigRed.  Let it simmer low and slow ‘til the cheeks turned pillowy soft and shred like warm butter. The end result? Deep color, killer bark, and a flavor that slaps whether it’s on a tostada, in a breakfast scramble, stuffed into a sandwich, or just straight off the board. Day 74: Back on trail… and straight into a fresh coat of snow We hit the trail again today hoping the rain from Quincy would’ve washed away the snow. Instead, we were met with a fresh, fluffy layer of it. Classic. But the sun was shining, spirits were high, and somehow we were loving it. It felt like stepping into a winter wonderland—until the wet socks hit. We postholed, we slid, Pablo launched himself into a snow angel, and then we hit the jackpot: dry trail. Actual dirt. Green hills. The joy was unreal. We ran. We skipped. We could feel our feet again. The descent into Belden was surreal, rail tracks, eerie resort vibes, and not a soul around. But then a beer on the riverbank and an unreal sunset meadow. It’s been a weird, wonderful ride. And we’re still walking. #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california #pctgrant #desert #thruhiking #pct #snow #hikertrash

Day 35: wet socks, wild plants & trail magic Started the day drying out my life after yesterday’s storm. Jetboil on. Socks hanging from bushes. Barefoot trip to the river to clean off the chaos. The climb out was hot. No shade. No real water. Just a cave with a “gratitude jar” inside. I wrote “shade,” obviously. Then came the poodle dog bush — looks chill, but apparently ruins your skin. Soon the whole trail was full of it. Like walking through a field of “don’t touch.” Somewhere between fake water sources and the Mojave views, I hit that thru-hike trance — tired, but moving. No idea how. Camped at Sawmill. Big hike uphill for water. Pablo handed me an apple. Fresh fruit is like gold. Simple things hit harder out here. See you tomorrow for Day 36. Still in shorts. 498.2/2650 total miles.  #pacificcresttrail #thruhike #pct2025 #scotland #california

Recipe using @LĒVO C machine: Ingredients 1 cup salted butter (softened) 4 cloves black garlic (mashed or finely chopped) 1 tbsp saffron flowers (dried petals) Instructions 1. Prepare the Saffron Infusion: Add the saffron flowers to the LEVO C machine's infusion chamber. You can use the built-in scale to measure about 1 tbsp of dried saffron flowers. Set the LEVO C machine to low temperature (around 160°F/71°C) for about 30-40 minutes to gently infuse the saffron flowers into the butter. 2. Prepare the Black Garlic: While the saffron infusion is happening, mash or finely chop the black garlic cloves to a paste. You can adjust the quantity based on your preferred intensity of black garlic flavor. 3. Infuse the Butter: After the saffron has infused, add salted butter to the infusion chamber of the LEVO C machine. Allow the butter to be infused for 30-40 minutes at a temperature of around 160°F/71°C. This will gently melt and infuse the butter with the saffron flavors. 4. Mix in the Black Garlic: Once the butter has finished infusing with saffron, remove it from the LEVO C machine and mix in the mashed black garlic. Stir well to ensure the garlic is evenly distributed throughout the butter. 5. Cool and Set: Pour the infused butter into a container or onto parchment paper, shaping it into a log or simply storing it in a dish. Allow the butter to cool and set in the fridge for at least 30 minutes. 6. Serve: Use your Black Garlic Saffron Flower Infused Butter on bread, roasted vegetables, pasta, or meats. Enjoy the rich, luxurious flavor! Kosher for Passover Chocolate Chip Cookies 🍪 No chill time. No mixer. Just mix, scoop, and bake. Ingredients: ½ cup brown sugar ½ tsp baking soda ½ tsp salt 1½ tbsp neutral oil 1 tbsp vanilla bean paste 1 egg, beaten (don’t skip this beat it first!) 2 cups almond flour ½ cup chocolate chips Instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Mix all ingredients together in a bowl by hand. It may feel dry. DO NOT add more liquid. Keep mixing with your hands and it’ll come together like Play-Doh. That’s exactly what you want. Scoop dough onto a parchment lined baking sheet and gently press the cookies down. Bake for 10–12 minutes if small, or up to 15 minutes for thicker cookies. Cookies may not brown. Don’t overbake, or they will turn into sand. For decades, the 16th Street Mall has been the heart of Downtown Denver, but years of wear and aging infrastructure led to a major city-led effort to revitalize the corridor. Now, after years of planning, reconstruction is well underway. Here’s what you need to know:  1️⃣ Project Overview: The 16th Street Mall Project is a $175.4 million revitalization of Denver’s most iconic pedestrian and transit corridor. The project aims to improve safety, enhance mobility, and upgrade aging infrastructure along 1.2 miles of 16th Street, from Market Street to Broadway. Work includes new granite pavers, tree plantings, enhanced public spaces, and transit improvements.  2️⃣ Why It Matters: This reconstruction will extend the lifespan of the Mall by 30-40 years while creating a more pedestrian-friendly and engaging downtown experience. The redesign includes more gathering spaces, shaded seating, and play features to encourage both tourism and local activity. It will also improve storm drainage and reduce costly maintenance issues that have plagued the corridor for years.  3️⃣ Construction & Status: The project is now 83% complete, with final phases of work continuing through Fall 2025. As of February 2025, reconstruction is complete between Market and Champa streets, with work continuing in multiple sections of the Mall. RTD’s Free MallRide remains in service but is temporarily rerouted to 15th & 17th Streets between Curtis and Civic Center Station.  🏗️ Development Team: * Led By: City & County of Denver * General Contractor: PCL Construction * Public-Private Partner: Downtown Denver Partnership * Funding: Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Denver Urban Renewal Authority (DURA), & GO Bonds  Stay tuned for more updates on this project and more from around Denver.  #16thstreetmall #denverdevelopment #downtowndenver #denvertransit #urbanrevitalization #publicspace #denverconstruction #rtd #mallride #denverprojects #denverinfrastructure #developingdenver

As a Naturopathic Doctor who focuses on supporting families with getting and staying healthy, one of my goals is to bring as much nourishment as possible in through diet. Just by making small changes like cooking more meala at home can significantly impact your family’s health! So today im going to share how easy it is to make homemade yogurt in an instant pot. Ingredients: 1 gallon milk (I use raw milk from a local farm) 1/4 cup yogurt starter (I used Maple Hill Organic Greek Yogurt) Tools needed: Instant Pot Thermometer Steps: 1. Put your milk in the instant pot and use the saute function to heat to 180 deg Fahrenheit. 2. Cool milk down to 110 deg Fahrenheit. I put my instant pot bowl into a bowl of ice water to cool it faster, but you can just let it sit.  3. Put your pot back into your instant pot and mix in your yogurt starter. 4. Press the yogurt button on your instant pot. Allow to sit for 8 hours at 110 deg Fahrenheit.  5. Strain the whey liquid off the top of your finished yogurt and store the yogurt in the fridge. Enjoy for up to 10-14 days!  Bonus: sweeten with a little honey, maple syrup, or fruit and enjoy with hemp seeds, chia seeds and any other toppings you love! #recipe #recipesoftiktok #healthyliving #naturopathicmedicine #naturopathicdoctor #holisticpediatrician #womenshealth

Day 38 — brutal climbs, surprise trail magic, and the town day I was dreaming of Woke up sticky and slow, tent damp from the night before and the sun already creeping over the ridgeline. My bag half-packed, my legs already protesting. Tehachapi was on the horizon — but it was going to make me earn it. Seven miles straight uphill to start, no shade, no warm-up, just pure trail honesty. Views opened up fast — dry valleys below, heat pressing in. Signed a trail register with a sweaty thumbprint and found the most random hiker rest stop: two chairs and a line of empty lockers in the middle of nowhere. Like a post-apocalyptic break room. No idea who set it up, but I owe them a thank you. Eventually the turbines appeared — a whole army of them spinning like they’d been waiting for me. The wind kicked up just in time to slap me around a bit, and the trail threw in a section that had completely washed out. Crossed it with the grace of a baby giraffe. Somehow stayed upright. Snack breaks, wild views, broken turbines laying on the ground like fallen giants. Crossed a bridge and just like that… Tehachapi. All that stood between me and food was a hitch in the wind. And then, trail magic. A kind soul scooped us up and dropped us at a hiker house that was actual heaven. Bikes ready to ride into town, cold drinks, good vibes. We hit a Chinese buffet like it was a mission. Five hikers. Four bikes. One rode handlebars. One sprayed whipped cream straight into their mouth back at base. Day 38 was endless sun, uphill battles, sketchy crossings, but worth every step. Town never felt so good. See you tomorrow for Day 39. #pacificcresttrail

In my five years of teaching, I’ve always paired hand movements with each letter sound of the alphabet to make learning more interactive and memorable for my kinders. But this year, I’m taking it up a notch by introducing movements for blends and digraphs, too! Here’s why: connecting a movement to a sound gives kids an extra layer of learning—it’s tactile, auditory, and visual all at once! And let me tell you, they’ve been loving it. In this reel, we practiced s blends by pairing each blend with a movement and then worked on decoding words together using backward decoding slides. Why backward decoding? It helps kids focus on the ending sounds of a word first, which is often where they get stuck. By decoding backwards, they build a stronger understanding of how sounds blend together, boosting their confidence and accuracy when reading. #teachersoftiktok #kindergarten #kinder #phonicsfun #sor #earlyliteracy #earlylearning #earlychildhood #literacyforall #scienceofreadingteachers #phonics #phonicsactivities

📝 review | HIGHERDOSE INFRARED SAUNA BLANKET 🔥 For years, I have wanted an at-home sauna as I felt I would use it more + save money in the long run from going somewhere to use one. I sat on that for a while because of 2 main reasons: 1️⃣ full infrared saunas are VERY expensive, especially the quality ones 2️⃣ the SPACE! Trying to find a room in someone’s home can be really hard + have the right plug-in for it. When I saw the @HigherDOSE sauna blanket, I did A LOT of research. I was a bit worried it wouldn’t give the full effect- but even though I do wish I had red light therapy with it, my main objective is really to increase circulation and sweat a little bit extra throughout my week. 📝 OVERALL: I absolutely love it. I think not only is it more cost-effective, but MUCH more space saving. I store mine in my coffee table, but a lot of people have used their closets or under their bed, easily. 🧼 CLEANUP: I 100% recommend also purchasing their sauna towels as it wraps around you like a layer to the sauna. Any time I use it, I rarely find any sweat left in the actual sauna after using. The only issue I have is it’s LARGE to always wash afterwards. I’ve also worn sweatpants + a sweatshirt without the blanket and have been ok. You can easily full open it after it’s cooled and just clean it that way. 🔥 HEAT: I would say my biggest complaint about this is I do wish it got a bit hotter BUT I do think it gets plenty hot. I just stay longer than usual, but I do like the levels. You don’t always need to get in it and sweat. If you just want to build a little body heat, set it on level 2 and enjoy. Right now I’m at levels 7/8 and it’s a good spot for me. 📲 MULTI-TASKING: personally, I actually prefer being able to do something while I’m in it. Compared to sitting in a full sauna just listening to a podcast or music, I can get work done, watch a movie, read a book, etc (without anything overheating lol) and it actually gets me to stay it it longer. That may just be me, but it’s a perk. - If you are interesting in purchasing, click the link in my bio as i have it saved for you! Did you know IV drug use can cause a heart infection? It might be a condition called infective endocarditis. You have to assume everything you put into your bloodstream will make its way to the heart. And that's where the bacteria or fungus can infect the tissue around one of your heart valves. An infected valve might allow for backflow or regurgitation. You see the problem. There’s a solution. Reach out for help to get sober. Balanced Meal for Baby! 👏🏻⭐️ When creating a balanced meal for a baby I aim to focus on three types of foods. ✅High-iron foods. If you have been following me for even a little bit, you know that adequate iron intake is a major goal when introducing solid foods to prevent iron deficiency. Providing a high iron food with every meal is recommended. Examples of high iron foods are beans, lentils, animal based products, sardines, eggs, tofu, etc.  ✅Vitamin C containing food. These foods tag team the high iron foods and aid in iron absorption. Most all fruits and veggies contain vitamin C and are also important for babies to be consuming for their vitamin and antioxidant content. Other vitamin C food sources are oranges, grapefruit, grapes, berries, collards, cantaloupe, raspberries, etc.  ✅Energy-Dense/Healthy Fat Food. We know that every bite counts when starting solids so choose a food option that contains tons of healthy fats and calories to help meet their nutritional needs. Fats are also recommended to be unrestricted for the first two years of life to aid in brain development! Examples of energy dense and healthy fat foods - avocado, sardines, cheese, olive oil, avocado oil, animal products, eggs, etc.  👉🏻Remember that some of these foods may overlap and meet both the high iron and the energy dense food requirement!  Use this simple method to create a balanced meal for your little one! But don’t worry if your little one isn’t always eating a balanced meal.  #blw #babyledweaning #babyledfeeding #foodforbaby #babynutritionist #infantnutritionist #infantnutrition #pediatricdietitian #dietitianforbaby #babyfoods #fyp #viral  #CapCut

Sweet Pineapple Steak Tacos One of Bachan’s newest flavors, Sweet Pineapple Japanese BBQ Sauce is now my new favorite marinade and topping!  Picked up a beautiful outside skirt steak from @k4gourmetbeef and I marinated it in that Sweet Pineapple sauce for 4 hours in the fridge. When ready to cook, wipe and pat the steak dry and let sit out for at least 20 min.  Dust it up with some sriracha seasoning to contrast the sweetness of the pineapple.  Fired up my Weber Searwood Smoker/Grill and cooked it for about 3-5 min per side over open flame. I greased my griddle insert with bacon fat and finished both sides with a nice char then pulled it off to rest for 10 min. While it’s resting, set heat to low to toast up your tortillas and melt the queso.  Sliced your skirt steak against the grain in 1/4 inch slices  Build your tacos with mango pico, steak and a healthy dose of that pineapple bbq sauce. Serve with pico and pineapple sauce on the side.  Mango pico recipe: 2 tomatoes diced  1 sweet onion diced 1 ripe mango diced 1/2 cup lime juice 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon minced garlic  Chopped cilantro to taste Let sit in fridge overnight #taco #steak #outdoorcooking #bachanspartner #jesus @Bachan’s @Bacon Up Bacon Grease @Weber Grills @K4Ranches

You can have normal hearing AND still struggle to make sense of the words. Auditory Processing Disorder (APD) is a condition where the brain has difficulty processing sounds, despite normal hearing.  Common signs:  ✅ trouble understanding spoken instructions, particularly in noisy environments ✅ difficulty distinguishing similar sounds ✅ frequent requests for repetition ✅ poor listening skills ✅ challenges in following conversations, especially in group settings.  ✅ People with APD may also struggle with reading, spelling, or remembering verbal information.  It’s important to note that APD does not involve hearing loss, but rather how the brain interprets sound. Like and follow for more ear things. When you drink, does it feel like you are walking on pins and needles? It might be a condition called alcoholic neuropathy. That translates to alcohol causing nerve damage. The bottom of your feet have thousands of nerve endings and they are very sensitive to touch, to temperature, to poison, and to malnourishment. Overconsumption of alcohol will damage nerves and deprive them of key nutrients. When these nerves get damaged, your feet start feeling funny. Balance troubles, pin and needles. Loss of feeling. You see the problem. There might be a solution. Seek help to Stop drinking immediately. See a neurologist and tell them how much you drink. Be honest so you two can create a realistic plan.  Healing happens. You can do it. Lamb Kofta - Ready in 15 minutes Ingredients: - 1 lb ground lamb (you can also use beef for this recipe)  - 3 to 5 cloves of garlic, minced finely - 1/4 to 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs - 1/2 white onion, grated - 1 tablespoon oregano  - 1 tablespoon cumin - 1 tablespoon paprika - 1/2 tablespoon cinnamon - 1/2 tablespoon kosher salt Method: - Place lamb into a bowl - Mince garlic and grate onion directly into the lamb - Mix breadcrumbs and all spices thoroughly  - Form into long logs and place skewers in the center - Broil on the top rack for 12 minutes, pulling out to rotate 3 to 4 times - Remove and let cool for a few minutes once browned and starting to get crispy Enjoy! #kofta #lamb #kebab #recipe #easyrecipe #yum #yummy #foodporn #dinner #easydinner #quickdinner #recipes #foodtiktok

Spaghetti with Roasted Cherry Tomato Sauce, Burrata Cream, and Basil - inspired by @rosannamarzialeofficial and prepared using my amazing @gozney  Serves: 4 Prep Time: 15 minutes Cook Time: 30 minutes Ingredients For the roasted cherry tomato sauce: 2 pints cherry tomatoes 4 cloves garlic, smashed 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil Salt, to taste For the pasta: 12 oz spaghetti Salt, for pasta water 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese Handful fresh basil leaves, torn For the burrata cream: 1 ball burrata (about 4 oz), torn into pieces 1/4 cup heavy cream Pinch of salt To finish: Extra olive oil, for drizzling Freshly ground black pepper (optional) Instructions Roast the Cherry Tomatoes Preheat your Gozney oven to high heat (around 750°F if using wood fire). In a cast iron pan or oven-safe dish, combine the cherry tomatoes, smashed garlic, olive oil, and a good pinch of salt. Roast for 10–15 minutes, until the tomatoes are blistered, caramelized, and just starting to burst. Stir occasionally. Remove from oven and lightly mash the tomatoes and garlic with a fork to form a chunky sauce, or blend with an immersion blender for an ultra smooth sauce. Cook the Spaghetti Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until al dente, according to package directions. Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water, then drain. Make the Burrata Cream In a small bowl, combine the torn burrata and heavy cream. Stir until smooth and creamy. Add a pinch of salt to taste. For an ultra-smooth texture, blend briefly with an immersion blender. Assemble the Pasta In a large bowl or skillet, toss the cooked spaghetti with the roasted cherry tomato sauce. Add a splash of reserved pasta water to help coat the noodles, if needed. Stir in grated Parmesan and torn basil leaves. Plate and Finish Twirl the spaghetti onto plates. Drizzle with burrata cream, finishing with a few extra basil leaves, a splash of olive oil, and freshly ground black pepper if desired. #italianfood #chef #italian #spaghetti #recipe

Training a puppy to sit is an important basic command that lays the foundation for further obedience training. Here are three tips to effectively teach a puppy how to sit: 1. **Use Positive Reinforcement:** Use treats or rewards that your puppy loves to encourage the behavior you want. Hold a treat close to your puppy's nose and slowly move it upwards and backwards over their head. As their nose follows the treat, their bottom will naturally lower into a sitting position. Once they are in the sitting position, praise them enthusiastically and give them the treat immediately. Repeat this process several times until they start associating the command with the action. 2. **Be Consistent:** Consistency is key in training. Use the same command each time you want your puppy to sit, such as saying "sit" in a firm but friendly tone. Avoid confusing your puppy by using different words or tones. Also, practice the training sessions in short bursts multiple times throughout the day rather than one long session. This helps reinforce the behavior and keeps your puppy engaged. 3. **Practice in Different Locations:** Once your puppy starts to understand the command in one location, gradually introduce distractions and practice in different environments. This helps your puppy learn to sit despite various distractions and reinforces their understanding of the command in different contexts. Start in a quiet environment at home, then gradually move to more challenging locations like the park or a busy street. Remember, patience and positive reinforcement are crucial. What is Resin?! What is Resin? Exploring the Aromatic World of Natural Gum Resins Resins are nature’s aromatic treasures, extracted from trees and plants around the world. In this video, we dive into the fascinating world of resins and their incredible uses in perfumery, incense, and traditional practices. Topics Covered: 🌟 Frankincense – Known as the “king of resins,” this fragrant substance from Boswellia trees offers woody, citrusy, and balsamic notes, often used for meditation and spiritual rituals. 🌟 Copal – A clean, pine-like resin from Bursera trees that is revered in Mesoamerican cultures. Learn why it’s a favorite for ceremonies and fresh, resinous fragrances. 🌟 Benzoin – Sweet and vanilla-like, this resin from Styrax trees is a staple in perfumery for its warm, balsamic aroma and excellent fixative properties. 🌟 Myrrh – Smoky, earthy, and mysterious, this resin from Commiphora trees has been treasured for centuries in rituals and as a key ingredient in oriental perfumes. 🌟 Labdanum – A rich, ambery resin derived from the Rockrose shrub, adding depth and warmth to many iconic fragrances. Discover how these natural gum resins are harvested, their unique scent profiles, and why they remain vital to perfumery and incense-making today! 🕯️ Don’t forget to subscribe for more insights into the art and science of fragrance. #Resin #Frankincense #Myrrh #Benzoin #Labdanum #Copal #Perfume #Incense #mybakhoor #fyp
